sections.content:
You know *como si* + imperfect or pluperfect subjunctive from B2 Unit 15. When explaining why a conversation or written message went wrong, *como si* captures the gap between what actually happened and how someone reacted.

Because *como si* always introduces a counterfactual or hypothetical comparison, it **never** takes the indicative or the present subjunctive:
• Use the **imperfect subjunctive** (*supiera, entendiera, fuera*) for an unreal comparison simultaneous with the main verb: *Respondió como si el comentario fuera literal*, *Habla como si no conociera el sobreentendido*.
• Use the **pluperfect subjunctive** (*hubiera leído, hubiera dicho*) when the unreal event would have happened earlier: *Me contestó como si no hubiera visto el guiño irónico.*

sections.title: Counterfactual comparisons in misunderstandings
rows: Reaccionó como si la ironía fuera un ataque literal.
Escribió como si no existiera ningún equívoco.
Respondió como si nunca hubiera leído el contexto.

items.spanish: Leyó el mensaje como si el sarcasmo fuera una afirmación literal.
items.english: He read the message as if the sarcasm were a literal statement.

items.spanish: Actuó como si no hubiera captado el guiño ni el sobreentendido de la frase.
items.english: She acted as if she had not caught the wink or the unspoken meaning of the sentence.

items.spanish: Contestó con tanta frialdad como si hubiera ocurrido un grave equívoco.
items.english: He replied as coldly as if a serious misunderstanding had occurred.

items.spanish: Habla de la ironía como si siempre resultara evidente por escrito.
items.english: She speaks about irony as if it were always obvious in writing.

sections.content: Never use the present indicative (*como si no sabe*) or the present subjunctive (*como si no sepa*) after *como si*. Choose between imperfect subjunctive (same time as the main verb) and pluperfect subjunctive (earlier than the main verb).
